caption:
"The clean energy transition is unstoppable. The question is whether the development transition will keep pace."
 
That was the defining message emerging from the UN High-Level Meeting on Critical Energy Transition Minerals and the thematic roundtables at #HLPF2026.
 
Demand for critical energy transition minerals is expected to almost triple by 2030, while around US$500 billion in new mining investment will be needed by 2040. Yet between 2020 and 2024, nearly 90 percent of new refining capacity for key critical minerals was added by a single leading producer for each mineral. The challenge is no longer only securing supply. It is creating more diversified, resilient and equitable value chains that also deliver development.
 
Throughout yesterday’s  discussions, one message resonated across governments, industry, international organizations, Indigenous Peoples and civil society:
The energy transition cannot repeat yesterday's extractive model.
 
Resource-rich countries should not remain exporters of raw materials while higher-value industries, technology and jobs are created elsewhere. Critical minerals must become a catalyst for industrialization, economic diversification, decent work and long-term prosperity.
 
The conversation has moved beyond principles. It is now about implementation. 
 
The Secretary-General's Guiding Principles provide the roadmap. The task now is to translate them into country-level action through stronger institutions, financing, technology transfer, local value creation and trusted international partnerships.
 
As co-chair of the UN Joint Task Force on Critical Energy Transition Minerals, together with UNCTAD and UNEP, and with UNDP leading the Country Support Mechanism, we are working with countries to turn these principles into practical support that strengthens governance, mobilizes investment and helps countries move up mineral value chains.
 
Critical minerals can power the energy transition if we ensure they also power development.

#EnergyforDevelopment #HLPF2026 #UNDP
